result:
Solution 1 is the only one I accept. I am relying on recalled facts about the classification of surfaces here and have not verified every step.

In characteristics 2 and 3 there are hyperelliptic surfaces with non-reduced Picard scheme. These have h¹(O_X) = 2 and trivial canonical bundle, so p₁ = p₂ = 1, yet they are not birational to abelian surfaces. For p ≥ 5, hyperelliptic surfaces have h¹(O_X) = 1, which rules out this kind of counterexample. This supports 5 as the smallest such prime. I did not check that no other surface types obstruct the claim for p ≥ 5, so that part rests on memory.

Solution 2 says 3, but the characteristic 3 counterexamples exist, so that is wrong. Its claim that the counterexamples are of general type is also unfounded. Solution 3 says 2, but characteristic 2 has counterexamples too, and its claim that only abelian surfaces occur for all p is false.

VERDICT 1: ACCEPT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
